evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database reports a Shang oracle-bone graph identified as 坐 only tentatively (“one possible reading”), and gives a different analysis for Warring States forms: 卩 over 土, interpreted as a kneeling person on the ground. It says Qin forms doubled 卩, and that the upper form was later corrupted so Shuowen misanalysed it as a remnant of 畱. It attributes the interpretation of ancient 坐 as kneeling/sitting and the proposed relation to 危 as proposals by Chen Jian. This conflicts with a simple continuous “two 人 sitting on 土” account; the source does not establish the proposed 危 relationship as settled.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database separately reports uses meaning seat/place, citing Han Feizi and Shiji; keeping watch, citing Zuozhuan and a Mawangdui manuscript; being implicated or convicted, citing Shiji and Hanshu; legal confrontation, citing Zuozhuan; and ‘because’, citing Yuefu and a Tang poem. These are dictionary-cited textual examples, not dates of the surviving manuscripts or proof that each sense developed directly from ‘sit’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 說文解字 entry reproduced by shuowen5.com
evidence.text: Shuowen defines 坐 as 止 (‘stop/remain’), analyzes it as 从土、从畱省, and says 土 is where one stops and the graph shares the idea of 畱. This is Xu Shen’s Han-period account, not independent confirmation of the graph’s earlier formation. The same page lists oracle-bone, Chu manuscript, Qin slip, Shuowen seal, and Han manuscript forms; its embedded image links were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 「坐」字的说文解字

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The source presents 坐 as meaning ancient kneeling-sitting, with citations to Zuozhuan and Liji, and separately records the seat/place, stay/guard, legal, and causal senses. It supplies no phonetic-component analysis for 坐; the dossier’s proposed 留 + 土 account is an ideographic-semantic account, not evidence for a sound component.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Shuowen5.com, reproducing Shuowen and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: Duan Yucai’s commentary treats 止 as ‘stop/remain’ and proposes extensions to settling/remaining, sitting on a mat, and more generally placing or resting something. This is an explicit historical lexicographic analysis, but it does not date each extension or demonstrate that every later sense (such as travel by vehicle or ‘because’) follows this path.
evidence.title: 「坐」字的说文解字

evidence.text: The entry cites Liji, Zuozhuan, Lunyu, Shiji, Han Feizi, and other works for sitting, place/seat, staying, legal implication, and causal uses. Its citations establish reported textual attestations, but the online entry does not date the manuscript witnesses; no chronology among senses is inferred from the gloss list.

gaps: The earliest identification of the Shang oracle-bone form as 坐 remains tentative in the inspected CUHK account; the listed oracle-bone reference乙2525/合1779 was not independently checked against a primary inscription image or excavation record.

The dossier’s ‘two people 从 sitting on 土’ explanation is not independently corroborated by the inspected ancient-form analysis. CUHK instead proposes 卩 + 土 in Warring States forms and corruption of the upper Qin form before Shuowen’s 畱 analysis; this account is itself reported as a scholarly analysis, not demonstrated here by direct glyph inspection.
The proposed relationship between 坐 and 危 as related forms/words is attributed to Chen Jian and remains a proposal in the source.
No component sound role was found, so component-by-component readings and a sound comparison are not applicable. No component or host local readings beyond 坐 were supplied or checked.
The Unicode character endpoint for U+5750 returned an internal error, so official character-specific kMandarin click-through verification failed despite the supplied local kMandarin row zuò.

Wikimedia Commons lists the seal glyph’s source lineage and permission note, but the raw SVG could not be opened; its exact depicted shape was not visually inspected. No local glyph extract is recommended from this single lead.

The consulted dictionary pages report classical source titles and quotations but do not provide manuscript witness dates or establish a securely dated earliest semantic attestation. Later extensions such as ‘ride/travel by’ were not chronologically demonstrated in this pass.
No evidence was found for whole-graph borrowing. The graph/word’s historical formation should not be described as a phonetic loan on the material inspected.
